title: Hosted endpoint PRD — deterministic sampling, cost-banding, and staged launch checklist
creator: Avery Chen
description: PRD for introducing deterministic sampling controls and a cost-banding pricing and routing model across hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Includes requirements, acceptance gates, scope adjustments, and a staged launch checklist for safe rollout.
problem_statement: Customers building deterministic workflows (e.g., automated grading, legal text generation, repeatable rerank pipelines) require a way to control sampling determinism across hosted endpoints while teams want explicit levers to trade cost vs. quality (cost-banding). Current hosted surface lacks a unified contract for deterministic outputs and no explicit pricing band that maps performance/latency guarantees to cost tiers.
goals: Expose deterministic sampling controls (seed + deterministic_mode) with clear behavioral contract for chat/completions and fallthrough behavior for embeddings/rerank
Introduce cost-banding tiers that map batch/quantization/backing-model profile to predictable per-token or per-embedding unit costs
Provide operational visibility and rollout gates so platform teams can measure quality regressions and customer impact during progressive rollout
Ship clear acceptance criteria and a rollback plan enabling safe canary traffic slices
non_goals: Change model training or weights; only serving/runtime behavior is in scope
Enforce identical deterministic outputs across model families (we provide compatibility guarantees, not exact parity across distinct architectures)
Price redesign for Dedicated or Private offerings — this PRD targets Hosted only
success_metrics: <=1% customer-reported nondeterminism incidents for deterministic_mode within 30 days of GA
95th percentile latency for deterministic tier within SLOs for each cost band
<0.5% increase in overall token cost for hosted fleet after enabling cost-banding (measured after 30 days, excluding customers opting into new bands)
Adoption: at least 10 customers opt into deterministic_mode or cost-banding during initial pilot
acceptance_criteria: API: new request fields seed (integer) and deterministic_mode (enum: off|soft|strict) documented and returning proper status codes for invalid combos
Behavior: deterministic_mode=strict produces repeatable token sequences for identical prompt+seed+model+params in same model-version within 99.9% of test prompts
Fallback: if strict mode cannot be satisfied (e.g., model variant mismatch), server returns structured error with recommended fallback (soft) and a trace id

Embeddings/rerank: deterministic_mode controls embedding generation's deterministic paths where supported; for non-deterministic backends the API returns deterministic_supported=false and a suggested migration path
Cost-banding: three bands (economy, standard, premium) have defined model variants, quantization profiles, max batch size, and documented per-unit pricing
Console: per-route telemetry surfaces cost-band usage, deterministic_mode adoption, and token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console
E2E tests: full automation harness with 2k synthetic prompts verifying determinism claims across supported models and bands
Operational: deployment runbook and rollback knobs implemented; canary slice steering and automatic abort on quality/regression thresholds
scope: Host API change, Console telemetry, runtime compatibility layer. Include chat, completions, embeddings, rerank endpoints. Exclude Dedicated pricing shifts and on-prem runtime changes beyond API contract.
scope_changes: 2026-02-20: Narrowed deterministic requirement from cross-architecture parity to intra-model-version determinism (decision: avoid brittle guarantees across model forks)
2026-02-28: Reduced initial cost bands from 5 to 3 to simplify billing integration after finance review
2026-03-05: Deferred deterministic guarantees for legacy quantized backends — flag deterministic_supported=false and provide migration doc
constraints: Runtime must support KV cache behavior that preserves seed-driven decoding for batched requests
Quantized kernels may not be able to provide strict bytewise determinism—expect platform-level compensations
Billing integration requires alignment with finance for per-embedding unit mapping before GA
rollout_checklist: Design: finalize API surface and sample request/response patterns in API catalog
Engineering: implement request parsing for seed and deterministic_mode with validation errors
Runtime: add deterministic flags to scheduler and ensure KV cache keys include seed and deterministic_mode
E2E QA: run determinism harness across nightly matrix (models x bands x prompt families)
Telemetry: Console dashboard for deterministic_mode adoption and cost-band usage created and validated
Pilot: onboard 3 pilot customers with SRE and solutions engineering support
Canary: progressive rollout 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated regression checks (quality, latency, errors)
Go/No-Go: run acceptance checklist and cross-functional review before GA
Post-GA: 30/60/90 day metrics review and retrospective
monitoring: Determinism regression alerts (if repeatability falls below threshold for canary)
Error rate increase in deterministic_mode requests
Billing anomalies for cost-banding (unexpected unit consumption spikes)
notes: Clarified that embeddings and rerank may only expose deterministic_supported flag for GA; full deterministic outputs for rerank to be revisited in Q3
Finance expects 2-week billing integration window — schedule in engineering roadmap
Enable opt-in pilot via account-level feature flag before exposing in self-serve console
